33021-the-carlovingian-coins-or-the-daug.title: The Carlovingian Coins Or The Daughters Of Charlemagne A Tal
33021-the-carlovingian-coins-or-the-daug.creator: Eugene Sue
33021-the-carlovingian-coins-or-the-daug.description: A book by Eugene Sue. The Age of Charlemagne is the watershed of the history of the present era. The rough barbarian flood that poured over Western Europe reaches in that age a turning point of which Charlemagne is eminently the incarnation.

79509-summer-camp.title: Summer Camp
79509-summer-camp.creator: Unknown
79509-summer-camp.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. nufactured in the United States of America SOFTCOVER LIBRARY, INC. 10017 TO PHIL—because it was promised.... ONE A whistle shrilled, echoing across the crystal-clear lake. Fifty young girls splashed and squealed their way out of the water. As the last wet little swimmer ran into the bathhouse, counselor Peggy Matthews climbed to the diving platform and moved gracefully along the board, her tanned limbs gleaming in the July sunlight. She stood statue-still, arms stretched behind her, chin held high, feet together.

arxiv-2111-08951.title: Exploring Student Representation For Neural Cognitive Diagnosis
arxiv-2111-08951.creator: Hengyao Bao, Xihua Li, Xuemin Zhao, Yunbo Cao
arxiv-2111-08951.description: Abstract Cognitive diagnosis, the goal of which is to obtain the proficiency level of students on specific knowledge concepts, is an fundamental task in smart educational systems. Previous works usually represent each student as a trainable knowledge proficiency vector, which cannot capture the relations of concepts and the basic profile(e.g. memory or comprehension) of students.

arxiv-2208-00194.title: Streaming Algorithms for Diversity Maximization with Fairness Constraints
arxiv-2208-00194.creator: Yanhao Wang 1 , Francesco Fabbri 2 , 4 , Michael Mathioudakis 3
arxiv-2208-00194.description: Abstract Diversity maximization is a fundamental problem with wide applications in data summarization, web search, and recommender systems. Given a set X X of n n elements, it asks to select a subset S S of k ≪ n k\ll n elements with maximum diversity , as quantified by the dissimilarities among the elements in S S .

arxiv-2308-06359.title: Low-Lying Zeros of a Thin Family of Automorphic L L -Functions in the Level Aspect
arxiv-2308-06359.creator: Matthew Kroesche
arxiv-2308-06359.description: Abstract Abstract. We calculate the one-level density of thin subfamilies of a family of Hecke cuspforms formed by twisting the forms in a smaller family by a character. The result gives support up to 1, conditional on GRH, and we also find several of the lower-order main terms.

arxiv-2503-23445.title: Design and Experimental Validation of an Autonomous USV for Sensor Fusion-Based Navigation in GNSS-Denied Environments
arxiv-2503-23445.creator: Samuel Cohen-Salmon & Itzik Klein
arxiv-2503-23445.description: Abstract This paper presents the design, development, and experimental validation of MARVEL, an autonomous unmanned surface vehicle built for real-world testing of sensor fusion-based navigation algorithms in GNSS-denied environments. MARVEL was developed under strict constraints of cost-efficiency, portability, and seaworthiness, with the goal of creating a modular, accessible platform for high-frequency data acquisition and experimental learning.

arxiv-2505-03926.title: Broadband acousto-optic modulators on Silicon Nitride
arxiv-2505-03926.creator: Scott E. Kenning, Tzu-Han Chang, Alaina G. Attanasio, Warren Jin, Avi Feshali, Yu Tian, Mario Paniccia, Sunil A. Bhave
arxiv-2505-03926.description: Abstract Stress-optic modulators are emerging as a necessary building block of photonic integrated circuits tasked with controlling and manipulating classical and quantum optical systems. While photonic platforms such as lithium niobate and silicon on insulator have well developed modulator ecosystems, silicon nitride so far does not.

arxiv-2511-17793.title: Attention Guided Alignment in Efficient Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2511-17793.creator: Shweta Mahajan, Hoang Le, Hyojin Park, Farzad Farhadzadeh, Fatih Porikli
arxiv-2511-17793.description: Abstract Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) rely on effective multimodal alignment between pre-trained vision encoders and Large Language Models (LLMs) to integrate visual and textual information. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of attention patterns in efficient VLMs, revealing that concatenation-based architectures frequently fail to distinguish between semantically matching and non-matching image-text pairs.

arxiv-2512-08956.title: DW-KNN: A Transparent Local Classifier Integrating Distance Consistency and Neighbor Reliability
arxiv-2512-08956.creator: Kumarjit Pathak, Karthik K, Sachin Madan, and Jitin Kapila
arxiv-2512-08956.description: Abstract K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) is one of the most used ML classifiers. However, if we observe closely, standard distance-weighted KNN and relative variants assume all ’k’ neighbors are equally reliable. In heterogeneous feature space, this becomes a limitation that hinders reliability in predicting true levels of the observation.

arxiv-2601-22362.title: Understanding Efficiency: Quantization, Batching, and Serving Strategies in LLM Energy Use
arxiv-2601-22362.creator: Julien Delavande, Regis Pierrard & Sasha Luccioni
arxiv-2601-22362.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Julien Delavande, Regis Pierrard & Sasha Luccioni. Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in production, contributing towards shifting the burden in terms of computational resources and energy demands from training to inference. While prior work has examined the energy cost of inference per prompt or per token, we highlight how system-level design choices - such as numerical precision, batching strategy, and request scheduling - can lead to orders-of-magnitude differences in energy consumption for the same model.

pmc-10643393.title: 68Ga-PSMA-PET/CT in addition to mpMRI in men undergoing biopsy during active surveillance for low- to intermediate-risk prostate cancer: study protocol for a prospective cross-sectional study
pmc-10643393.creator: William Gondoputro, Paul Doan, Athos Katelaris, Matthijs J Scheltema, Bart Geboers, Shikha Agrawal, Zhixin Liu, John Yaxley, Richard Savdie, Kris Rasiah, Mark Frydenberg, Matthew J Roberts, David Malouf, David Wong, Ron Shnier, Warick Delprado, Louise Emmett, Phillip D Stricker, James Thompson
pmc-10643393.description: BackgroundIn active surveillance there is significant interest in whether imaging modalities such as multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) or 68Gallium prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography/computerized tomography (68Ga-PSMA-PET/CT) can improve the detection of progression to clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) and thus reduce the frequency of prostate biopsies and associated morbidity.

pmc-10693064.title: Construction and validation of a nomogram to predict the overall survival of small cell lung cancer: a multicenter retrospective study in Shandong province, China
pmc-10693064.creator: Ziqian Song, Hengmin Ma, Hao Sun, Qiuxia Li, Yan Liu, Jing Xie, Yukun Feng, Yuwang Shang, Kena Ma, Nan Zhang, Jialin Wang
pmc-10693064.description: BackgroundPatients diagnosed with small cell lung cancer (SCLC) typically experience a poor prognosis, and it is essential to predict overall survival (OS) and stratify patients based on distinct prognostic risks.MethodsTotally 2309 SCLC patients from the hospitals in 15 cities of Shandong from 2010 − 2014 were included in this multicenter, population-based retrospective study.

pmc-11454062.title: 9307 Significance of Assessing QTc Interval in Chronic Hypoparathyroidism and its Clinical and Biochemical Correlates
pmc-11454062.creator: Preeti Vijay Namjoshi, Soma Saha, Vibhav Sharma, Ravinder Goswami, Rajiv Narang, Kalaivani Mani
pmc-11454062.description: Disclosure: P.V. Namjoshi: None. S. Saha: None. V. Sharma: None. R. Goswami: None. R. Narang: None. K. Mani: None. Background: Patients with chronic hypoparathyroidism (cHypoPT) and hypocalcemia are at risk of QTc prolongation and life-threatening arrhythmias. Information on clinical and biochemical correlates of QTc in cHypoPT is limited. Design: Observational study in cHypoPT cohort, tertiary-care-center.

pmc-11602052.title: Canine uropathogenic and avian pathogenic Escherichia coli harboring conjugative plasmids exhibit augmented growth and exopolysaccharide production in response to Enterococcus faecalis
pmc-11602052.creator: Grayson K. Walker, M. Mitsu Suyemoto, Megan E. Jacob, Siddhartha Thakur, Luke B. Borst, Kwame Kumi Asare, Kwame Kumi Asare, Kwame Kumi Asare
pmc-11602052.description: Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) and avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) are extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli (ExPEC) that infect dogs and poultry. These agents occur both as single-species infections and, commonly, in co-infection with Enterococcus faecalis (EF); however, it is unclear how EF co-infections modulate ExPEC virulence.

pmc-11710782.title: Investigating the role of SORL1 in mediating AD‐specific endolysosomal phenotypes in neurons and microglia
pmc-11710782.creator: Brooke A. DeRosa, Yalun Zhang, Charles G. Golightly, Lauren Coombs, Lauren E. Rothschild, Brian W. Kunkle, Michael L. Cuccaro, Jeffery M. Vance, Margaret A Pericak‐Vance, Peter St George‐Hyslop, Derek M. Dykxhoorn
pmc-11710782.description: BackgroundDysregulation of endolysosomal trafficking is a major pathogenic mechanism in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). From the family of AD‐linked endosomal pathway genes, SORL1 stands out as one of the highest risk factors. SORL1 encodes an endocytic sorting receptor that mediates endosomal trafficking and processing of key AD‐associated molecules, including pathogenic forms of amyloid‐β (e.g., Aβ42) and amyloid precursor protein (APP).

pmc-12391324.title: Deciphering chromatin domain, domain community and chromunity for 3D genome maps with Mactop
pmc-12391324.creator: Ran Duan, Dachang Dang, Shichen Fan, Shaowen Yao, Shihua Zhang
pmc-12391324.description: Advanced high-throughput chromosome conformation capture techniques, like Hi-C, reveal genome organization into structural units like topologically associating domains (TADs), which are crucial in gene expression regulation. While accurately identifying TADs is vital, distinguishing different types of TAD boundaries and TAD categories remains a significant challenge in genomic research.

pmc-13314119.title: Foodborne antimicrobial resistance risks in traditional markets in West Sumatra: a one health investigation of Escherichia coli in chicken meat
pmc-13314119.creator: Engki Zelpina, Prima Silvia Noor, Yurni Sari Amir, Suliha Suliha
pmc-13314119.description: Background: Escherichia coli is a prevalent bacterial contaminant in poultry meat, functioning as an indicator of fecal contamination and antibiotic misuse in animal husbandry. The rising prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) E. coli strains is a significant concern for food safety and public health, especially in areas where traditional markets are the primary meat distribution channels.
